title: Black Bean & Cottage Cheese Enchilada Bake
displayTitle: Black Bean & Cottage Cheese Enchilada Bake
seoTitle: Black Bean & Cottage Cheese Enchilada Bake | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Corn tortillas layered with black beans, cottage cheese, and enchilada sauce
subtitle: Corn tortillas layered with black beans, cottage cheese, and enchilada sauce
description: Corn tortillas layer with black beans, corn, and a cottage cheese filling under melted cheese and a chili-spiced tomato sauce, then bake into sliceable squares. It is a stacked casserole, not rolled enchiladas, so it serves a crew fast.

steps.title: Heat the oven and build the filling
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Warm olive oil in a skillet over medium, cook onion 5 minutes until soft, then add garlic, chili powder, and cumin and cook 1 minute more. Target oven/smoker temperature: 375°F.

steps.title: Combine the filling
steps.instruction: In a large bowl, combine the onion mixture, black beans, cottage cheese, and corn kernels. Stir until evenly mixed.

steps.title: Layer the bake
steps.instruction: Spread a thin layer of sauce in a greased 9x13 pan. Layer tortillas, a portion of filling, more sauce, and a scatter of cheese. Repeat to build 3 layers, finishing with sauce and the remaining cheese on top.

steps.title: Bake until bubbling
steps.instruction: Bake 35–40 minutes until the cheese is melted and golden and the center is hot throughout. Target oven/smoker temperature: 375°F.

steps.title: Rest before slicing
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares so the layers hold together instead of sliding apart.

steps.title: Top and serve
steps.instruction: Top with green onions if using and serve with extra salsa or hot sauce on the side.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover black bean and cottage cheese enchilada bake — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool enchilada bake and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Squeeze excess liquid from thawed corn if using frozen so the bake doesn't turn watery.
Rookie tip: Rest the full 10 minutes — cutting immediately out of the oven makes the layers collapse.
Add diced jalapeño to the filling for a spicier version.
tonightSpread: Main: Black bean and cottage cheese enchilada bake
Sides: Simple green salad, Mexican street corn

Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.

Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Reheat squares covered at 350°F until warmed through rather than microwaving dry.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It is a hands-off oven bake that happens to be vegetarian and protein-dense, and it holds and reheats in squares just like the crew's usual casserole nights.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: assemble up to a day ahead and refrigerate unbaked. Storage: refrigerate baked squares up to 4 days. Reheating: cover and reheat at 350°F until warmed through, about 15 minutes.
substitutions: Use pinto beans instead of black beans.
Use flour tortillas if corn tortillas aren't on hand.
Use Greek yogurt instead of cottage cheese if texture is a concern — blend it smooth first.
